reason: The week-12 stagflationary dispersion book has worked in its first week on every main leg: XLE +2.57% (XLE +2.7% on 10-09 alone, top sector, +42.6% YTD per tapeboard.com), IWM short +1.57% (small caps were the weakest index on 10-07, -1.31%), COMT +1.98%; weighted leg P&L is about +1% with no stop near being hit. Research (two web searches plus tapeboard.com daily recaps for 10-07 and 10-09, a single source I could not cross-check) shows WTI ~$90-92, the 10-year stuck at ~5.24-5.28%, VIX down to 14.84. The catalyst calendar favors the book as built: September CPI prints Wed 10-14 with headline nowcast ~3.6-3.7% (up from 3.4%), and the 10-27/28 FOMC carries a live hike risk. A hot print supports energy and commodities and hurts small caps and duration. The TLT short is only -1.13% against an 8% stop and is the direct expression of that CPI/hike risk, so I keep it. VIXY is decaying (-1.45%), but with VIX at 14.8 the tail is at its cheapest right before a binary macro week; at 8% it is a defined-cost hedge against my short-IWM/long-cyclical gross. I hold rather than trim, because a full or partial rebalance costs real basis points and nothing in the data has falsified any leg. The existing stops (XLE 13, IWM 10, COMT 12, TLT 8, VIXY 25) and take-profits stay as the risk framework, with 22% cash earning 4%.
